assessment.nobel_worthiness: KPZ theory revealed universal structure in driven fluctuations through a simple stochastic growth mechanism, with exceptional explanatory reach.
assessment.attribution: Kardar and Zhang represent formulation of the theory; Takeuchi precise experimental confirmation of its fluctuation predictions.
assessment.maturity: The core universality class has mature rigorous and numerical development and substantial experimental support in suitable regimes.
uncertainties: The packet lacks a complete original-author history and specific independent tests; neither every growth process nor every dimension shares the same behavior.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Minimal collective-motion models and hydrodynamics explain how active particles generate ordered motion, identifying a general nonequilibrium mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek represents the minimal model; Toner and Tu the continuum theory.
assessment.maturity: The framework is mature and extensively investigated numerically and experimentally in active systems.
uncertainties: The packet provides no specific quantitative tests. Biological complexity and model-dependent transitions should not be subsumed under one universal claim.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal symmetry made critical fluctuations exactly analyzable and exposed universality across two-dimensional statistical systems.
assessment.attribution: The supplied trio represents the foundational shared conformal-field-theory breakthrough.
assessment.maturity: The theory and its critical-model predictions are mature and extensively tested.
uncertainties: The packet does not delimit joint foundations from later individual advances or identify which experimental systems satisfy the assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Jamming gives an intelligible collective mechanism for the onset of rigidity in disordered assemblies, with broad relevance to soft and granular matter.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel represent the organizing framework and its development.
assessment.maturity: Core model phenomenology is mature, supported by substantial simulations and experiments.
uncertainties: The packet does not define frictional, thermal and geometric regimes or establish full collaborator credit. One critical picture should not be presented as a complete account of all amorphous solids.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical self-consistency supplied a tractable framework for strong electronic correlations, connecting model mechanisms to observed material behavior.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar represent dynamical construction, Vollhardt the infinite-dimensional theoretical basis.
assessment.maturity: The framework has a mature record of numerical use and experimental comparison.
uncertainties: The packet omits full contributor priority and does not distinguish exact limiting results from approximate finite-dimensional implementations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Global quantum-phase structure identifies a simple general mechanism behind measurable interference and transport effects.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov represents the electromagnetic phase effect; Berry general adiabatic geometric phases. Their discoveries are related but distinct.
assessment.maturity: Both effects have extensive independent experimental and mature theoretical foundations.
uncertainties: The compound scope requires a precise citation and potentially divided recognition; complete original attribution is not supplied.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topology identified a robust organizing principle for electronic insulators and linked it to observable boundary transport.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele represent classification and prediction, Molenkamp quantum-spin-Hall realization.
assessment.maturity: The central time-reversal-invariant phase is established and has sustained theoretical and experimental impact.
uncertainties: The packet provides no complete priority record or exact boundary between this achievement and subsequent topological phases.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controllable lattice gases made many-body statistical mechanisms experimentally accessible, providing direct tests where ordinary calculation is limited.
assessment.attribution: Zoller represents theoretical model engineering; Bloch and Greiner defining experimental realization and imaging.
assessment.maturity: The foundational lattice-simulation and Mott-transition results have extensive independent experimental development.
uncertainties: The packet lacks a detailed contribution history and does not distinguish initial bosonic realization from later fermionic and microscopy developments.
